llm.summary: This skill is an audit and rollback tool, but it exposes powerful local operations and sensitive snapshots with weak controls.

dimensions.detail: The web dashboard binds to 0.0.0.0 on port 8080 in multiple server variants, and one Flask server runs with debug=True; administrative APIs lack visible authentication.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is mostly manual, but the setup script can add persistent shell aliases to ~/.zshrc and start a dashboard server in the background; this is disclosed, not hidden.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions encourage shell and OpenClaw execution wrapping and include destructive deletion examples; rollback is marketed as instant recovery while the artifacts also admit limitations and the code shows incomplete or fragile recovery behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists operation logs, permission rules, alerts, and snapshots under ~/.openclaw, can snapshot sensitive paths including ~/.ssh, and stores copied snapshot content in Git history.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The audit, dashboard, permission, snapshot, and rollback capabilities fit the stated purpose, but the implementation gives broad command execution, rollback, permission-rule mutation, and snapshot access without adequate guardrails.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Only run it on a trusted machine, do not expose port 8080 to a network, avoid using it with privileged accounts, remove ~/.ssh and whole-home snapshots from defaults, and treat rollback as experimental rather than a backup. Do not copy the destructive examples into real directories.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: Raw shell and deletion examples relate to the skill's audit and recovery purpose, but repeated rm/rm -rf examples are unsafe documentation for a tool that claims reliable rollback.
[TP4] unexpected: The concern is supported in substance: the artifacts make strong security and rollback claims while code inspection shows unauthenticated admin APIs, incomplete rollback behavior, and weak permission enforcement.
[T05] unexpected: The server exposes administrative endpoints for snapshots, rollback, alerts, and permission rules on all network interfaces without visible authentication or authorization.
[T09] unexpected: The dashboard renders stored operation and alert fields through innerHTML, and the shell wrapper embeds user-controlled command text into Python heredocs before eval execution.
[T05] unexpected: Snapshot behavior is overbroad: automatic paths include ~/.ssh, and one snapshot manager defaults to recursively hashing the whole home directory when no path is supplied.
